time_plan.30m: Check for any official Treasury/White House statement or credible press report confirming a Bessent departure; if none, treat the market move as noise. Watch SPY and ES futures tick.

predictions.reasoning: Scott Bessent, Treasury Secretary, is widely regarded as a market-friendly, fiscally pragmatic voice who reassures investors on tariffs, debt issuance, and tax policy. A sharp jump in the implied probability of his departure would likely be read as a loss of a stabilizing moderate and raise policy-uncertainty premia, pressuring broad equities modestly risk-off. However, a prediction-market probability shift alone, absent an actual confirmed resignation headline, is a weak and noisy driver; equity reaction to a single cabinet official — even Treasury — is typically muted and well below the 700bps tradable threshold.

predictions.reasoning: Treasury Secretary turnover introduces uncertainty around debt management, FX policy stance, and fiscal credibility, which can modestly weaken the dollar on a confirmed exit. But the link is weak and second-order; absent a confirmed resignation the prediction-market move carries little informational force, and dollar reaction to cabinet rumors is usually negligible. Direction is tentative — in some scenarios safe-haven flows could even support the dollar, making this genuinely mixed.

evidence_used: Market question concerns departure of Scott Bessent, current US Treasury Secretary, before 2027
Bessent's public reputation as a market-friendly, moderate steward on tariffs, debt issuance and tax policy
General empirical pattern that single-cabinet-official rumors produce muted, sub-1% moves in broad US assets absent confirmation
uncertainty_notes: A prediction-market probability shift is not a confirmed event; without an official announcement the informational content is low
Direction of dollar reaction is genuinely ambiguous (policy-uncertainty weakness vs safe-haven strength)
Magnitude almost certainly below the 700bps tradable threshold, so neither prediction is actionable under the stated rule

llm_justification.summary: A sharp rise in the implied probability that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent leaves the administration would plausibly be mildly risk-off for US equities and modestly dollar-negative, since Bessent is viewed as a stabilizing, market-friendly policymaker. But the mapping is weak: absent a confirmed resignation headline the prediction-market move is a noisy sensor, and historical cabinet-rumor reactions in liquid US assets are small — well under the 700bps tradable bar. Both predictions are low-confidence and effectively non-tradable research signals.
key_assumptions: Bessent remains perceived as a net-stabilizing, market-friendly figure whose exit raises policy uncertainty
A probability spike reflects genuine leaked information rather than market noise or manipulation
Broad ETFs (SPY, UUP) are the cleanest liquid proxies for the diffuse policy-uncertainty channel
failure_modes: The departure may already be public/priced, so no fresh asset move occurs
The prediction-market move could be noise or thin-liquidity manipulation with no underlying news
A single Treasury Secretary change may have negligible effect on broad indices, making the proxy exposure too weak to register
Direction could reverse if a market-friendly successor is simultaneously signaled, or if safe-haven flows support the dollar rather than weaken it
Magnitude expected far below 700bps, so treating this as tradable would be a false signal
